Acclimate

AK-luh-mayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To acclimate is to become accustomed to a new climate, environment, or situation.

Astronauts spend weeks in a special facility learning to acclimate to the disorienting effects of weightlessness before launch.

Worked Example

Deep-sea divers must acclimate slowly to increasing water pressure, or risk serious injury on the way back up.

Acclimate is about the gradual process of adjusting to a new physical or situational condition.

How Strong Is It? — get used to → acclimate → assimilate

get used to vs. acclimate

get used to vs. acclimate: Get used to is a casual, everyday way to describe adjusting to something, less formal than acclimate.

assimilate vs. acclimate

assimilate vs. acclimate: Assimilate means to fully absorb into a new culture or environment, an even deeper adjustment than simply acclimating.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ac-

prefix — ac-: to, toward (Latin ad-)

root — climate

root — climate: climate (Greek klima, 'region, zone')

Put it together

Put it together: Acclimate comes from ac- ('to, toward') + climate -- literally 'to adjust toward a climate.'

Use the root in a new word: climate
